## Summary

**Scenario:** `scenario-043cffd4d852512e` — Node backend, `vehicle-b-rudder` on `coupled6` plant, 30 s duration (0.1 s timestep, 77 steps), single waypoint mission to (20 m north, 0 m east).

**Run:** `run-539cda64-dbb0-4827-8d6e-e9df67b41d1e` — completed successfully in 7.7 s wall-clock.

**Metrics:**
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Propulsion energy | 2.976 J (movement-only) |
| Total sensor cost | 41.195 |
| Total energy (propulsion + sensor) | 44.171 |
| Steps | 77 |

Note: sensor cost dominates total energy here even though no sensors were explicitly configured in this scenario — this reflects whatever default/oracle instrumentation cost the backend attributes to the run; if you want a pure propulsion comparison, use `propulsion_energy` (2.976 J).

**Evidentiary status — important caveat:** The `vehicle-b-rudder` preset carries validation status **`model-structure-trajectory-scored-fail`**. Per its validation claim: the MMG model structure was scored against six measured MARIN single-screw KVLCC2 trajectories (using measured rudder/RPM inputs), and the literature-coefficient parameterization **failed** the precommitted trajectory/IMO tolerances. Critically, **no evidence validates the Vehicle B USV-scale coefficients** actually used in this run.

**Bottom line:** The simulation executed correctly and produced numerically consistent metrics, but the underlying vehicle dynamics model for `vehicle-b-rudder` is not validated at USV scale and has failed its own precommitted validation test at ship scale. Treat these energy/trajectory results as illustrative of the simulator's mechanics only — **not as validated predictions of real vehicle-b-rudder behavior.**
